source: Daily Investment Brief Macroeconomic Dashboard + authoritative-source supplementation
sourceStatus: Daily Investment Brief remains the primary dashboard layer, but automated retrieval continues to expose client-side placeholders ('Analyzing...' / '--'). No values are inferred from placeholders. MacroMicro remains supplemental where accessible. Current gaps are filled with official BLS/ISM/Federal Reserve/FRED evidence and current Reuters/market reporting. The retired legacy macro dashboard is not used.
methodology: Directional channels are scored from -2 to +2. Dashboard readings are inputs, not trading signals. Creator/video/social claims have zero direct score weight until independently verified. Fundamental holding scores do not move mechanically with macro/theme strength.
regime: Resilient US jobs and services demand are colliding with record refined-product inflation and still-restrictive long rates. August payrolls reversed part of the prior Waller relief: yields and hike pricing rose, gold weakened tactically, while physical AI/power capex remains strongly expansionary.

channels.label: Growth / Demand
channels.regime: Resilient jobs + strong services + expansionary manufacturing
channels.interpretation: August payrolls +162k with upward prior revisions materially improve the broad-demand picture on top of ISM Services 55.4 and Manufacturing 54.6. Growth is resilient rather than booming, but recession-style demand assumptions are not supported.

channels.label: Policy Relief
channels.interpretation: The payroll surprise pushed September hike odds back toward the high-50s/around 60%. Services Prices 72.6 and record diesel keep the Fed constrained; Waller's prior tactical relief is partly reversed.

channels.label: Financial Conditions
channels.regime: Long and short yields restrictive again
channels.interpretation: The 2Y rose toward 4.37% and the 10Y touched roughly 4.81% after payrolls. Financing remains expensive for housing, leveraged projects and long-duration equities despite accessible capital for quality issuers.

channels.label: Broad Credit
channels.regime: Open for quality; costly for marginal borrowers
channels.interpretation: Quality issuers retain access, but higher risk-free rates and AI/utility capital competition raise project hurdle rates and keep deposits/cash conversion important.

channels.label: Weak-End Credit Stress
channels.interpretation: The last verified CCC-and-lower yield reference around 14.6% remains punitive but dated. The direction of weak-borrower refinancing stress is unfavorable; the exact live level is not inferred.

channels.label: Consumer
channels.regime: Employment resilient; fuel and financing squeeze persistent
channels.interpretation: Better payrolls and participation support incomes, but record diesel and high borrowing costs still pressure financed discretionary demand. Treat the consumer as resilient but squeezed, not collapsing.

channels.label: Housing
channels.interpretation: Long rates rose again after payrolls and mortgage affordability remains poor. Housing and leveraged property activity remain clear macro laggards.

channels.label: Industrial / AI / Power Capex
channels.interpretation: Official ISM evidence continues to validate large transmission/generation investment, material purchasing and long-lead planning. Prefer booked orders, named customers and FCF conversion over headline requested MW.

channels.label: AI Memory / Bandwidth
channels.regime: Near-term constrained supply; supply-response clock active
channels.interpretation: Memory/electronic components remain constrained and capacity is shifting toward next-generation AI. Future supply additions remain the main medium-term cycle risk.

channels.label: Input Costs
channels.regime: Energy, services and industrial cost pressure extreme
channels.interpretation: Services Prices 72.6, Manufacturing Prices 71.1, record diesel and tight copper/electrical/electronic/memory inputs keep cost pressure at the top of the range.

channels.label: Labour
channels.regime: Broad payroll evidence improved despite services hiring caution
channels.interpretation: NFP +162k, unemployment 4.1% and upward revisions outweigh the contractionary ISM Services Employment index for the broad macro signal. Hiring is resilient rather than hot.

channels.label: Risk Appetite
channels.interpretation: S&P -0.38%, Nasdaq -0.29% and Dow -0.51% are modest risk-off, while semiconductors and small caps showed pockets of resilience. This is not a broad liquidation.

channels.label: Crude
channels.regime: Hormuz security premium + tight physical routing
channels.interpretation: Brent $92.68 and WTI $91.48 remain elevated after a strong week. Hormuz traffic is exceptionally depressed, but demand destruction and future de-escalation remain the main reversal risks.

channels.label: Refined Products
channels.regime: Record diesel scarcity remains dominant inflation channel
channels.interpretation: US diesel near $5.85/gal and persistent distillate stress keep refined products more important for inflation and margins than crude alone.

channels.label: US Gas / Global LNG
channels.regime: Strategic LNG value; US gas still comparatively contained
channels.interpretation: Henry Hub around $2.98 is supportive but not a generic US gas scarcity signal. Contracted LNG infrastructure retains strategic value as buyers diversify supply.

channels.label: Gold / Monetary Hedge
channels.regime: Structural hedge intact; tactical confirmation weakened
channels.interpretation: Gold fell about 1.2% after payrolls pushed yields and USD higher. Long-run fiscal/geopolitical hedge logic remains, but near-term entry again depends on real yields and inflation data.
